raw_case_text:
A 28-year-old male presented with complaint of blurring of vision in the left eye (LE) and headache for 15 days. He had a history of DF 22 days before the presentation. The DF was confirmed by positive immunoglobulin M enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay serology for the Dengue virus. His best-corrected-visual-acuity (BCVA) was (right eye [RE]) 6/9 and (LE) finger counting 0.5 m. On examination, (LE) fundus revealed focal constriction of arteries and veins, soft exudates, dot-blot and flame-shaped hemorrhages in branch vein distribution, attempt at macular fan formation, and area of macular edema [Figure 1]. (LE) optical coherence tomography (OCT) revealed neurosensory detachment with cystoid macular edema [Figure 2]. Central macular thickness was 1018 mu.
Complete blood count revealed platelet count: 84,000 (thrombocytopenia). Based on history, thrombocytopenia and clinical findings, diagnosis of dengue retinopathy was made. The patient was given intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide (4 mg/0.1 ml).
At 2 months, BCVA (RE) was 6/6 and (LE) 6/18. Since (LE) visual acuity did not normalize, fundus fluorescein angiography (FA) and OCT angiography (OCTA) were done. FA LE showed normal foveal avascular zone (noted in the early phase of angiogram), few areas of the delayed filling (inferotemporal vascular arcade) with capillary leakage. Disc leakage was also noted [Figure 3]. OCT showed cystoid spaces, intraretinal exudates with back-shadowing, disruption of the external limiting membrane, the ellipsoid zone, and the interdigitation zone in the foveal region. There was the subfoveal area of hyperreflectivity and retinal thinning [Figure 4]. (RE) OCTA was normal. OCTA (LE) showed distortion of retinal superficial and deep capillary plexus (SCP-DCP) inferotemporal to foveal center [Figure 5]. The features on OCT and OCTA were suggestive of AMN.
Six months visit revealed complete resolution of fundus features, visual acuity of both eyes on Snellen's 6/6, but with persistent micropsia. OCT revealed retinal thinning with the restoration of retinal layers. Distortion of SCP-DCP on OCTA persisted, which was the only persistent defect explaining the visual complaint of the patient [Figure 2].

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old male presented with blurring of vision in the left eye (LE) and headache for 15 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed blurred vision in the left eye and headache of 15 days' duration, beginning approximately one week after an episode of acute febrile illness diagnosed 22 days prior to presentation.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of acute febrile illness (dengue fever) 22 days prior to presentation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for left-eye blurred vision, headache, and persistent micropsia at follow-up.

objective.physical_examination: Initial ophthalmic examination showed best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of 6/9 in the right eye (RE) and finger counting at 0.5 m in the left eye (LE). LE fundus examination revealed focal constriction of arteries and veins, soft exudates, dot-blot and flame-shaped hemorrhages in a branch vein distribution, an attempt at macular fan formation, and macular edema. At 2 months, BCVA was 6/6 (RE) and 6/18 (LE); at 6 months, BCVA was 6/6 in both eyes with complete resolution of fundus features.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count revealed thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 84,000. Initial LE optical coherence tomography (OCT) showed neurosensory detachment with cystoid macular edema and central macular thickness of 1018 mu. At 2 months, fundus fluorescein angiography (FA) of LE showed a normal foveal avascular zone in early phase, delayed filling in the inferotemporal vascular arcade with capillary leakage, and disc leakage; OCT showed cystoid spaces, intraretinal exudates with back-shadowing, disruption of the external limiting membrane, ellipsoid zone, and interdigitation zone in the foveal region, subfoveal hyperreflectivity, and retinal thinning; OCT angiography (OCTA) was normal in RE and showed distortion of the retinal superficial and deep capillary plexus (SCP-DCP) inferotemporal to the foveal center in LE. At 6 months, OCT showed retinal thinning with restoration of retinal layers and persistent SCP-DCP distortion on OCTA.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Dengue retinopathy complicated by acute macular neuroretinopathy (AMN), confirmed by positive dengue virus IgM capture ELISA serology 22 days prior, thrombocytopenia, and characteristic OCT/OCTA findings. Treated with intravitreal triamcinolone acetonide (4 mg/0.1 mL). At 6-month follow-up, fundus features completely resolved and Snellen visual acuity recovered to 6/6 bilaterally, with persistent micropsia corresponding to residual SCP-DCP distortion on OCTA.
